_comment: Tier B: the DEVELOPER-RUN audio corpus. These recordings are copyrighted, so the files are NOT in the repository (`.gitignore` excludes public/e2e/) and this manifest is the record instead. It exists so that (a) every number computed from this audio is reproducible by anyone holding the same bytes — the hashes are the contract — and (b) a clone WITHOUT the files can see exactly what it cannot measure, rather than silently measuring less. Guarded by tests/ai-pipeline/tierB.manifest.test.ts. Tier A (fixtures/tier-a/) is the committed, CI-runnable half and is honestly limited to speech-like, word-less material.

files.truthQuality: version-exact — 229.0s LRC against 228.98s audio, so its offset is OURS

covers: the clean case: best offset in the corpus (-0.02s)
files.truthQuality: version-matched (203s entry against 218.77s audio is an edit difference the median-offset fit absorbs; its residual offset is -0.02s, the best in the corpus)

covers: the ALTERNATE-TAKE case: ~30 lines with no evidence anywhere
files.truthQuality: ONE-SIDED — a 237s edit against 233.57s audio, so its offset is partly a version difference and cannot be attributed to us
version-matched, but only 16 of 47 lines carry enough matched evidence for the offset fit — the rest are transcription-bound

covers: Japanese, THE FIRST TAKE live arrangement
stem path that measurably HURTS (15.4s vs 2.8s mix)
files.truthQuality: no LRCLIB entry exists for the First Take arrangement; truth is YouTube caption onsets (±2s), in tests/ai-pipeline/akfg-ground-truth.test.ts

covers: sung Japanese, but NOT used by any committed test
a song with NO committed transcript, so its evidence must be produced locally
an ORPHANED truth fixture: no test in the suite consumes it
files.truthQuality: matched, but scored by NO test, and its lyric sheet was derived from this very LRC (31 of 31 lines byte-identical with the timestamps stripped), so the text is circular — see the ledger on orphaned fixtures

covers: the isolated vocal of the hardest song — the only place the documented word-mode RAMP was ever measured
a clean stem, for the acoustic-verdict calibration (ledger L15: stem verifies 5.5x more lines than the mix at equal p90)
